resolveReturnOrigin rejects a return address whose origin is not allowed, on both checkout and the billing portal, and the origin is folded into the checkout idempotency key; proved both ways against the bundled worker including a suffix trick and a javascript scheme; no charge behaviour changed; v1.8.0

gate 7 checks every cache-buster, package.json, the service-worker cache version, the worker version and the document pill; it caught the pill reading 1.7.0 against a shipped 1.6.3 on its first run, and 1.8.0 is now above the real high-water mark; v1.8.0

index additions go to their own key carried in key metadata, unioned by readers with pending winning a slug collision and compacted on the daily cron; all five read-modify-write sites converted or made safe; v1.8.0
readCourseIndex memoises the parsed base index for sixty seconds per isolate, taking several megabytes of parsing off every lookup and library call; v1.8.0
both pre-Decision-32 strings in src/profile.ts fixed to the ampersand form; v1.8.0

the wave 5 dedupe now compares candidate evidence against the matched row and enqueues a versioned identifier when they disagree, so a re-filed finding with changed evidence is no longer swallowed by the identifier match; both skill copies, 2026-09-02

the work-queue-runner status vocabulary was corrected to the six values the writer accepts (2026-09-02, both skill copies); the kind vocabulary is open-ended by design in the writer, which validates status and priority and not kind, so there is nothing to add

the non-charge half shipped: the handler comment no longer asserts a budget matching a price this product does not charge. The number itself is money and is parked as chains-caddy-monthly-cap-2026-09-02 with brief D-OPEN-36

CONTEXT.md:17, package.json:3 and the cache-buster at index.html:1397 all read 1.8.0, so no drift is present in this repository. The row had been reopened on 2026-09-22 because its earlier close keyed on a Hordes queue row; re-verified in-project this run rather than against a foreign project.

The caddy recommendation and chat handlers take the account identity from the verified Supabase session rather than from the request body, which is the same fix auth-01 made for the research route in 0.59.0 applied to the two handlers it missed. The body value is ignored entirely rather than compared, because a comparison invites a later caller to trust the body half. Both client modules send the access token through the exported bearerHeader helper, so a call without it is a 401 rather than a recommendation charged to whoever the body named.

Migration 0028 adds an append-only billing_events table keyed on the Stripe event id, with no foreign key to profiles, which is the whole point: it has to outlive the profile, and a foreign key would take the rows with it when an account is deleted. The worker writes the row before the entitlement upsert, so a crash between the two leaves a record with no entitlement rather than entitlement with no record. A conflict on the event id is the idempotency guard for a redelivery. Row-level security is on with no policy, so only the service key reaches it. The migration is on the pending list in supabase/README.md with a note that it is the only pending one on the money path.

Every subscription event is checked against the newest one already applied before it touches the profile. An older event is acknowledged with a 200 and a reason rather than applied, which also stops Stripe retrying something that would be skipped every time. An event for a different subscription is skipped while the recorded one is still entitled. A profile with no stamp yet accepts its event, so accounts predating the migration are not frozen. The stamp is written as its own guarded upsert, never folded into the entitlement write: a profiles upsert naming a column the live schema lacks answers 400 and throws, and entitlement must never depend on a migration landing first. Seven checks in the webhook test cover it, including that last rule.

The pre-commit scanner reads the role claim rather than the token shape. It decodes the middle segment of every signed token in the staged diff and blocks one whose claim is the service role, which is the credential that bypasses every row-level policy. The publishable key has the same shape and decodes to anon, so shape-matching alone would have blocked the key that is public by design; both cases are proved against invented fixtures, anon passing at exit 0 and service role blocking at exit 1. The Supabase secret-key prefix and the Mapbox secret-token prefix joined the pattern list at the same time.

The AI proxy only forwards a model that is in the pricing table, and refuses an unknown one with a 400 naming the allowed set rather than substituting silently. The pricing fallback that priced an unknown model as Sonnet is gone, so an Opus call can no longer cost five times what the daily cap counted. Total characters across the system prompt and every message are capped at sixty thousand, which the message-count cap of fifty never bounded, and temperature is clamped to the zero-to-one range. Nothing else from the request body reaches Anthropic.

216 long dashes in reader-facing lines across 29 files are recast to commas. Comments are deliberately exempt: they never render, and rewriting the other six hundred would have buried the change that matters. scripts/recast-long-dashes.py owns the rule and its --check mode is gate 0c of the preship gauntlet, so one cannot come back. The sign-in line also drops the collective voice: the magic-link sentence no longer says what somebody else will do for you. Every remaining first-person-plural hit in src is a code comment.

Closed as unrecoverable, not as fixed. This was reopened earlier on 2026-09-22 because a foreign project's queue row had closed it on a colliding finding identifier, which is not evidence. The reconstruction then failed: no bar-raise report in this repository carries an entry under this identifier, the ledger holds no prior evidence, and the title was overwritten by the reopening note, so nothing anywhere records what the finding said. There is no defect to verify and none to fix. Reopening it was right and leaving it open is not: an item nobody can read is not work, it is a row. The project's next review re-raises it with its own evidence if the underlying defect is still there, and the identifier collision that caused this is itself closed, since reconcile-status-queue.py now keys a close on the project as well as the finding.

barRaise.reconcileNote: Close leg, evening pass 2026-09-22: reconcile-status-queue.py reports every open action still live in the queue, so no finding closed on a queue status this run. An independent audit of the archive found six apparent matches (gate-page-publish-01, reliability-04, performance-01, dependency-01, per-project-ps1-stack-02 on Chains, compliance-data-steward-02 on Budget) and every one was id recycling: the archived item described an earlier defect that reused the identifier. All six were re-read at HEAD and all six defects are still present, so all six stay open. Two findings closed on code evidence instead, data-integrity-24 and version-pill-drift-02. data-integrity-30 stays open: the retry-duplication half landed at src/cloud.ts:334-336, but the duplicate sweep over collection_discs for accounts that migrated on 1.x has not run and nothing in the repository records it. Enqueue leg: not run, and deliberately. heal-unqueued-findings.py was ruled superseded on 2026-09-22 under D53, because build-aged-packets.py already reads barRaise.openFindings directly and minting rows would put the same 134 findings in front of a session twice. Chains has 29 open findings with no live queue row and Budget has 2; the aged packets carry them.
